props.title: Get Over It
props.initialSlug: Teen retells Shakespeare in modern high school crush

sections.content: Get Over It reimagines Shakespeare's "A Midsummer Night's Dream" through the lens of high school romance, following a trend of teen Shakespeare adaptations that peaked in the late 90s and early 2000s. Like 10 Things I Hate About You (1999) and She's the Man (2006), it modernizes classical literature for young audiences. The film stars Ben Foster as Berke Landers, who joins the school musical to win back his ex-girlfriend, inadvertently finding himself in a complex romantic quadrangle reminiscent of Shakespeare's beloved comedy.

sections.content: The early 2000s teen movie renaissance brought fresh energy to classic stories. Cruel Intentions (1999) turned "Les Liaisons Dangereuses" into a prep school drama, while Romeo + Juliet (1996) gave Shakespeare's tragedy a vibrant modern setting. Get Over It distinguishes itself through self-aware humor and meta-theatrical elements, with Martin Short's scene-stealing performance as the flamboyant drama teacher Dr. Desmond Forrest Oates.

The film's soundtrack captures the era perfectly, featuring performances by Sisqó and Vitamin C alongside original songs from the musical-within-the-movie. This musical element connects it to other teen performance-centered films like Save the Last Dance (2001) and Center Stage (2000), where artistic ambition intertwines with romantic storylines. sections.content: Get Over It bridges the gap between traditional teen comedies and the musical renaissance that would follow with High School Musical (2006) and Hairspray (2007). Its blend of theatrical performance and teen romance anticipated the success of shows like "Glee" and films like Pitch Perfect (2012), proving audiences' appetite for young performers tackling both contemporary and classical material.
